summary: 2025 chapter (PubMed 41242767): neuroimaging/electrophysiology of hypnosis is 'highly heterogeneous, limiting the establishment of a consistent neurophysiological framework.' Proposes componential (multi-mechanism) approach: induction effects vs suggestion effects vs susceptibility effects.
content: 2025 chapter (PubMed 41242767, 'Neural dynamics of hypnotic responding: From unique to multicomponent perspectives'): 'despite robust behavioural evidence supporting the concept of hypnotic responding, findings from neuroimaging and electrophysiological studies have been highly heterogeneous, limiting the establishment of a consistent neurophysiological framework.' Proposes a COMPONENTIAL approach: hypnotic process comprises multiple distinct interacting mechanisms — (a) large-scale network connectivity changes from induction, (b) localized modulations from specific suggestions, (c) individual susceptibility amplifying responses. Additional variability from individual differences beyond susceptibility. Keywords: Altered state of consciousness; Hypnosis; Hypnotic responding; Hypnotic susceptibility; Neurophysiology.
